About

**Justice Adjei Owusu** is a PhD student at **North Carolina A&T State University (NCAT)** with a deep interest in AI research and V2X communication. His work blends advanced ML algorithms with real-world system modeling. He spends considerable time studying the **mathematical foundations** behind these models.

🧪 Research Focus

Justice’s current PhD research centers on intelligent transportation and robust machine learning, with an emphasis on:

• V2X Communication

Designing systems that enable vehicles, infrastructure, and edge devices to exchange information efficiently and reliably.

• Reinforcement Learning (RL)

Developing RL-based decision-making agents, with attention to stability, robustness, and real-world feasibility.

• SUMO Traffic Simulation

Using the SUMO microscopic traffic simulator to evaluate ML-driven traffic control strategies in realistic, large-scale urban settings.

• Digital Twins for Intelligent Transportation

Creating virtual replicas of road networks and communication systems to safely test algorithms before deployment—
an approach increasingly used by leading AI and automotive research labs.

⚡ Additional Expertise

Beyond his core transportation-AI research, Justice also contributes to:

  • Energy policy and planning
  • Energy system reliability and resilience analysis
  • Mathematical modeling for engineering systems

🎯 Long-Term Vision

Justice aims to work with top AI research teams both in industry labs or global technology companies to advance:

  • Robust and mathematically grounded ML systems
  • Safe and interpretable AI for critical infrastructure
  • ML-enabled transportation and energy solutions
